items.title: Vanderbilt University — BYOD ransomware claim
items.summary: BYOD claims it locked Vanderbilt's databases and took data including Social Security numbers. Ransom notes appeared on campus machines and staff were asked to shut their devices down; Vanderbilt has not confirmed the scope.

items.title: Texas Health and Human Services — BYOD claim
items.summary: The same BYOD group claimed an attack on the Texas Health and Human Services agency on Monday. No independent confirmation yet.

items.title: Maersk — WhiteArmor demands $5M
items.summary: Maersk confirmed a breach of a legacy system it inherited through an acquisition. WhiteArmor says it took about 100GB of logistics and supply-chain data and is demanding $5 million.

items.title: Tanner Clinic (Utah) — Incransom claim
items.summary: Incransom listed Tanner Clinic, a Utah healthcare provider, on its leak site on November 12. The claim has not been independently verified.

items.title: Computacenter — Incransom claim
items.summary: Incransom also claimed the IT services provider Computacenter, which creates possible downstream exposure for its managed-service customers. Unverified.

ransomware.note: All of these are group claims. Use the victims' own disclosures as the authoritative record.

items.title: Microsoft 365 global outage — Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams
items.summary: A global Microsoft 365 outage began on November 12. It peaked at about 140,000 Downdetector reports from 74 countries, with Exchange Online mailbox access failing. Recovery was finished in Asia-Pacific first and was still being extended to other regions on November 13 (EX1550543 / MO1550821).

items.title: M365 outage spills into Teams, SharePoint, Copilot and Defender XDR
items.summary: Reports of the outage broadened to Teams, SharePoint, Copilot and Defender XDR, and to UK services. Third-party M365 integrations, including Claude's, were also affected.

items.title: Cloudflare Durable Objects incident
items.summary: Cloudflare had a separate, brief incident on November 13 involving errors in its Durable Objects service, fixed quickly. There is no confirmed link to the Microsoft outage.

items.title: AWS denies outage reports
items.summary: Amazon said AWS was working normally all day and blamed an unrelated disruption elsewhere for inaccurate news reports. It is a reminder to check provider health dashboards before invoking a DR plan.

items.title: Google Cloud London zone power-loss lessons (Oct 20)
items.summary: Background item: a third-party facility hosting europe-west2-b lost utility power, and a controller fault stopped the backup generators from starting. It is a useful case study of single-zone dependency.

outage.note: The M365 outage was still in partial recovery outside APAC when this edition was written.

items.title: CISA KEV adds GPUStack, FreeSWITCH, OpenSSH, IBM Aspera Faspex
items.summary: On November 9 CISA added four actively exploited flaws to KEV, including OpenBSD OpenSSH and IBM Aspera Faspex. Federal agencies had until November 12 to remediate and do forensic triage.

items.title: Ivanti Connect Secure — CVE-2026-111357 / CVE-2026-118527
items.summary: CISA ordered agencies to fix two exploited Ivanti Connect Secure flaws. The deadline for CVE-2026-118527 is today, November 13.

items.title: Node2Shell flaw now exploited
items.summary: CISA warns that attackers are now exploiting the critical Node2Shell vulnerability in the wild.

items.title: Zyxel GS1900 switch zero-day (CVE-2026-107441)
items.summary: A zero-day was reportedly used to take over about 1,000 Zyxel GS1900 switches. Check for exposed management interfaces.

items.title: Apple iPhone CVE-2024-27834 added to KEV
items.summary: CISA added the older iPhone flaw to KEV with an 18 November due date. One source links it to APT29 targeting of older devices.

items.title: Cyclone Murasu landfall — Andhra Pradesh, India
items.summary: Cyclone Murasu made landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 3, the second cyclone to hit there in less than a week.

items.title: Ecuador flooding
items.summary: Heavy rain and flooding across Ecuador had killed 12 people and affected 56,323 as of November 5.

items.title: Santa Catarina, Brazil storms
items.summary: The Santa Catarina state government reported 671 storm-related incidents across 76 municipalities on November 4–5.

items.title: El Niño-driven Pacific typhoon season
items.summary: Pacific cyclones have caused more than 230 deaths since April, while the Atlantic has had its calmest start since 1941.

items.title: M 6.4 — 30 km WSW of Lata, Solomon Islands
items.summary: A magnitude 6.4 earthquake on November 9, with a green PAGER alert and no tsunami.

physical.note: There was only one significant earthquake this week. US wildfire coverage in the results was from September, so it was left out.
